subject: Follow-up: Pilot plan for long-document summarization and regression guardrails
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Tran <lisa@medlynx.ai>, Chris Park <chris.park@medlynx.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Pilot plan for long-document summarization and regression guardrails

Hi Lisa / Chris —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the MedLynx clinical reporting flow and the examples of long discharge summaries. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the pilot kicks off: 

Summary of call
- Goal: Accurate, extractive-friendly summaries of 8–20k token clinical notes with minimal hallucination and strong section-preservation (Hx, Meds, Assessment).
- Constraints: latency target <= 600ms for 2k windows; tolerable up to 1.5s for full 20k-window once batched.
- Primary concerns you raised: truncation of context affecting medication lists, and occasional summarization hallucinations that change dosages.

Proposed pilot scope (2-week technical POC)
1) Data: 150 de-identified reports you’ll share (we received the upload link) + 50 synthetic edge cases from Redwood.
2) Eval matrix: summarization fidelity (ROUGE-L, Section-F1), hallucination rate (manual span-check), token latency/throughput, and truncation exposure (fraction of summaries missing final sections).
3) Models to evaluate (fast pass):
   - redwood-long-concat-v2-16k (default Redwood long-window optimized model)
   - redwood-quant-13b-32k (aggressive quant with 32k context for full-window fidelity)
   - llama3-70b-q4f (baseline open checkpoint your infra is familiar with)
   Notes: we’ll also test a hybrid split approach that summarizes chunks and then stitches + final refinement to guard against lost trailing sections.
4) Prompt sets and canary prompts: we’ll run a curated prompt set (attached) that targets medication lists, follow-up tasks, and diagnosis extraction.
5) Rollout guardrails: automated section checks, alert on medication list mismatch, canary on 5% of production traffic with human-in-the-loop for any regression above threshold.

Deliverables and timeline
- Day 0–2: ingest data and baseline runs.
- Day 3–6: run model sweep + generate benchmark artifacts (we’ll share results in Drive).
- Day 7–10: iterate prompts and quantization settings, run regression tests.
- Day 11–14: final recommendation and 2-hour review workshop with your engineering + clinical leads.

Attachments: pilot-prompt-set-20260915.txt (prompt set + canaries) — I attached a stub here; full prompt pack in Drive.

Next steps / asks for you
- Confirm the 150-file upload is complete (I saw 102 so far).
- Tell us if there are any immutable constraints (e.g., exact latency SLO under 500ms) or additional redlines on hallucination risk.

I’ll loop in Monica and Neha for ops/CS coordination; Monica — can you schedule the workshop for week of Sep 28 if pilot finishes on time?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this rolling.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Thanks Ben — this looks good and captures the call. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Data upload — we’ll finish the last 48 files by EOD today.
2) Latency — our internal target for summaries that are surfaced directly to clinicians is 750ms for the 2–4k common cases; >1s is acceptable for full 20k only if we can batch efficiently.
3) On models: Chris asked whether the "redwood-quant-13b-32k" approach retains medication fidelity versus a chunk+stitch flow — any early intuition? Also, we need to ensure any quantized option has deterministic output for auditability.

Also CC'ing our engineering manager, Chris, to loop him in on the workshop scheduling.

On the regression side, we will require a short audit trail that links any summarized span back to source tokens (or at least source section IDs) for the first production week.

—Lisa

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pilot plan for long-document summarization and regression guardrails

Lisa — thanks, and that’s a helpful latency note. Quick answers and some specifics for the bench we’ll run tomorrow: 

On medication fidelity:
- Quantized long-window (redwood-quant-13b-32k) keeps token-level fidelity for most numeric and enumerated spans in our internal tests, but we do see a small increase in substitution errors versus full-precision when the text is highly noisy (OCR-artefacts, inconsistent abbreviations).
- Chunk+stitch + refinement reduces missing trailing-section issues (med lists at end) but introduces stitching artifacts unless you use a final extractive verification pass — we’ll include a section-F1 extractive verifier in the pipeline.

Determinism and auditability:
- For the pilot we can pin seeds and temperature=0 for deterministic runs.
- Redwood can provide token offsets in the response metadata when running the redwood-long-concat-v2-16k model; for the quantized variants we’ll return best-effort offsets and a confidence score per span.

Recommended bench configuration (we will run these permutations):
1) redwood-long-concat-v2-16k — chunk size 16k, overlap 256 tokens, prompt template A (attached).
2) redwood-quant-13b-32k — full 32k window, temp=0, top_p=1.0; evaluate medication substitution errors separately.
3) chunk+stitch (llama3-70b baseline) — 8k chunks, stitch via fusion prompt, then extractive verifier.

Metrics we’ll report back in the Drive folder (link below): ROUGE-L, Section-F1, medication-precision/recall, hallucination-rate (span-level), latency p50/p95/p99, and truncation-exposure rate.

Attached are the prompt set and a small sample benchmark CSV with a few rows from our internal sanity runs (longdoc-benchmarks-20260916.csv). The prompt pack includes specific canary prompts to catch dosage hallucination and missing trailing medication lists.

Guardrails we suggest for production: 
- Canary rollout (5% traffic, human review on flagged cases)
- Automatic section-presence checks — failover to extractive baseline if medication list missing
- Regression alert: fail pilot if medication-precision drops >2% vs baseline or hallucination-rate increases >1.5%

Links and artifacts:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-longdoc-benchmarks
- HubSpot: HS-9876543

Monica / Neha — can you confirm we have the infra playbook ready for returning offsets and confidence scores? If not, we’ll scope a tiny adaptor for the pilot.

Thanks — I’ll queue the sweep now and send the first artifacts by tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Ben

Attachments: longdoc-benchmarks-20260916.csv (CSV results stub, 8 KB), pilot-prompt-set-20260915.txt (12 KB)
